editorial.headline: Writing Is Open Nationally—But Not to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans literary and technical writing nationwide, yet Bali’s PMA moratorium closes the registration route for a Bali address.
editorial.body:
**Activity 90111 is the professional home of the written work itself.** It covers writing and editing undertaken by individual writers, whether the work is credited to them or prepared for someone else, and whether it is fiction or nonfiction, printed or digital. Short stories and novels sit comfortably within that remit, as do scripts for film, television, radio, computer games and animation. Independent blogging, technical writing, poetry and comparable literary creation are included too. The focus is authorship and editorial craft: creating the words, shaping the text and developing the written work.

That focus matters because it draws a practical boundary around the activity. It is not the production, reproduction or distribution of books and music, nor translation for book editing, nor the work of independent musicians and actors in video or audiovisual content. For founders, the relevant question is therefore whether the business being registered is centred on writing, editing and literary creation. The activity is open across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. It can accommodate a solo author or editor as readily as a larger writing-led operation, provided the registered activity remains within that written-works remit.

Nationally, the PMA position is unequivocally open. The status is **TERBUKA**, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In other words, the national entry does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. But Bali changes the registration reality sharply. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA at a Bali address today. The Bali record identifies the Besar scale as low risk, and the provincial PMA moratorium blocks all low- and medium-low-risk activities for a Bali address. The restriction is island-wide and permanent under the stated Bali rule.

This is not a contradiction in the national record; it is a location-specific constraint on PMA registration. The national framework remains open to full foreign ownership, while the Bali position is recorded as **Closed (Bali moratorium)**. For a writing, editing or literary-creation venture, that distinction is the central fact: the activity is nationally open, but a Bali-address PMA registration is blocked by the moratorium. The business concept may be literary, technical, digital or script-based; the decisive Bali issue is the risk-based moratorium applied to the registration address.
